reason: Provider admission (#559) rewrote every resumed turn to routing, so approval, results-callback, subagent-wait and final-answer-retry resumes skipped their parked step; late recorded receipts never reached the ledger; a turn resuming itself while settling was refused; deleted queued turns broke Core startup; complete() leaked the execution claim on an approval pause; and recovery held provider slots idle. The selection covers admission and scheduler contracts (test_chat_throughput), resume through start_provider_turn for approval, callback, subagent wait and final-answer retry, restart recovery and read repair (test_chat, test_chat_subagents, test_process_results_webhook, test_turn_prompt_cache, test_in_turn_context_pruning), the stream/complete and hook paths (test_chat_tool_loop, test_native_hook_turn_ends, test_reasoning_replay, test_history_content_fidelity), conversation delete and API streams (test_chat_api, test_storage, test_chat_workspace, test_chat_catchup), and the journeys that start or settle provider turns (goals, queue, schedules, agent messages, turn outcomes). It includes every test #559 left red in these files and the browser companion screenshot replay node whose stand-in lacked the ledger reader.
exclusions: Full suites are not approved and are excluded. No UI, Playwright, native or frontend code changed, so those layers are empty. Excluded because they were already red before #559 and are unrelated to this change: tests/v3/test_chat_final_synthesis_recovery.py (nameless tool-call fragment test, red at 0095d77^) and tests/v3/test_chat_leftovers.py (three test_routing_commentary_stops_at_an_unreadable_frame_beside_a_real_call cases). Only the screenshot replay node of tests/v3/test_browser_companion.py is selected; its real-Chromium capture test needs a browser the Python job does not provide. The approval resume was also exercised against a scratch Core with a real OpenRouter model.
